recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the FHIR-31900 clarification in current core source; any stronger recommendation about using Task.requestedPeriod for fulfillment-task deadlines should be a separate work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-31900 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and asked to clarify Task.restriction by limiting it to fulfillment of another Request resource, adding an invariant requiring a fulfillment Task code and focus, revising Task.restriction.period, and distinguishing that period from task timing/deadline concepts.
initial_application: Git commit 6ea83c0de2 applied the issue by adding the tsk-1 invariant, Task.restriction comment, and Task.restriction.period definition/comment. The current source retained the invariant using code 'fulfill' and focus, but the period usage note still said executionPeriod represented requested timing, retained the old period.high due-date note, and misspelled ServiceRequest.occurrence[x].
additional_context: FHIR-34136 later added Task.requestedPeriod for desired task timing and documented executionPeriod as actual execution timing. FHIR-28397 later refined the Task.restriction comment while preserving the fulfillment-request limitation. FHIR-37001 addressed the code binding concern created by the FHIR-31900 invariant and was already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Updated source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml to reference Task.requestedPeriod and Task.executionPeriod correctly, removed the contradictory due-date note, corrected ServiceRequest.occurrence[x], and updated source/task/task.svg only to mirror that spelling in the generated-looking diagram tooltip.
source_changes: source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml: corrected Task.restriction.period definition spelling and revised the comment to distinguish requestedPeriod, executionPeriod, and restriction.period.
source/task/task.svg: updated the Task.restriction.period tooltip spelling from ServiceRequest.occurance[x] to ServiceRequest.occurrence[x] to align with the authoritative StructureDefinition.

related_jiras.note: Added Task.requestedPeriod and established the requested-time versus actual-execution distinction used to reconcile the FHIR-31900 period note.
Later replaced the Task.restriction comment with narrower fulfillment-request wording while preserving FHIR-31900's limitation.
Addressed the Task.code binding issue raised by the FHIR-31900 invariant and was already represented on the combined branch.
